note: Subjects/Maths/M1 Mechanics 1/1 Mathematical models in mechanics.md
outline: Mechanics replaces objects and contacts with idealised models. A particle has mass but negligible size; a lamina has negligible thickness; a rigid body does not deform. Light means negligible mass, uniform means evenly distributed mass, and inextensible means fixed length. Smooth contact has no friction, while rough contact may have friction. A light smooth pulley with a light string gives equal tension on both sides. A bead is constrained to a wire; a peg is a fixed support. Choose each assumption for the property relevant to the problem.

misconceptions.refutation: A particle has mass, but its dimensions are negligible for the problem.
misconceptions.contrast: A vehicle can be treated as a particle when only its motion along a route matters.

misconceptions.statement: A light rod or string has zero tension or force.
misconceptions.refutation: Light means its mass is negligible; it can still transmit a force.
misconceptions.contrast: A light string can pull with non-zero tension.

misconceptions.statement: A smooth surface or pulley has no normal reaction or tension.
misconceptions.refutation: Smooth removes friction, not the normal reaction or the tension in a string.
misconceptions.contrast: A block on a smooth table still experiences a normal reaction.

misconceptions.statement: Uniform means the same as light or rigid.
misconceptions.refutation: Uniform describes even mass distribution; light describes negligible mass and rigid describes no deformation.
misconceptions.contrast: A uniform heavy rod may be rigid and has its centre of mass at its midpoint.

misconceptions.statement: Inextensible means the string cannot move.
misconceptions.refutation: Its length stays constant; different parts can still move.
misconceptions.contrast: For a taut inextensible string over a fixed pulley, connected particles have equal displacement magnitudes.

items.stem: State what is meant by treating a body as a particle.

rubric.point: It has mass but negligible dimensions for the problem.

items.explanation: The body retains its mass; its size and shape have no effect on the motion being modelled.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: State what is meant by a lamina.

rubric.point: A thin flat sheet whose thickness is negligible compared with its other dimensions.

items.explanation: A thin flat sheet whose thickness is negligible compared with its other dimensions.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: State what is meant by a rigid body.

rubric.point: Its shape and size do not change under the forces considered.

items.explanation: Its shape and size do not change under the forces considered.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: Find the property represented by a light rod.
items.explanation: Light means negligible mass, so the rod can still transmit force. Equal mass distribution describes a uniform rod.
hints: Focus on what the model simplifies.
Separate mass, size, and deformation.
Check which physical property the adjective describes.

items.stem: State the difference between a uniform rod and a non-uniform rod.

rubric.point: A uniform rod has mass evenly distributed along its length.
A non-uniform rod does not have mass evenly distributed along its length.

items.explanation: A uniform rod has constant mass per unit length, so its centre of mass is at its midpoint. A non-uniform rod need not have its centre of mass there.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: State the two assumptions for a light inextensible string.

rubric.point: Its length remains constant when pulled taut.

items.explanation: Light removes the string’s own weight from the model. Inextensible means it does not stretch; tension may still be present.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: Find the force that a smooth horizontal table can exert on a resting block.

options.A: A normal reaction but no friction.
options.B: Neither a normal reaction nor friction.
options.D: A fixed friction force and a normal reaction.

items.explanation: Smooth means frictionless contact. The table can still exert a normal reaction on the block.
hints: Focus on what the model simplifies.
Separate mass, size, and deformation.
Check which physical property the adjective describes.

items.stem: State what a rough surface permits that a smooth surface does not.

rubric.point: A rough surface can exert friction tangential to the contact.

items.explanation: Rough contact can exert friction; its size depends on the situation. Smooth contact has no friction.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: State the assumptions of a light smooth pulley.

rubric.point: There is no friction between the pulley and the string.

items.explanation: The pulley’s mass and bearing friction are neglected. With a light string, the tension is the same on both sides of a smooth pulley.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: Find what inextensibility implies for two particles joined by a taut string over a fixed pulley.

options.A: They have equal displacement magnitudes along the string.

items.explanation: The total taut string length is fixed, so one end moving a given distance makes the other end move the same distance along the string. The particles can move and may have different masses.
hints: Focus on what the model simplifies.
Separate mass, size, and deformation.
Check which physical property the adjective describes.

items.stem: State what is meant by a bead moving on a wire.

rubric.point: A small object is constrained to move along the wire.

items.explanation: A bead is modelled as a small object threaded on a wire; its path is constrained by the wire. Contact friction depends on whether the wire is specified as smooth.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: Explain how a peg differs from a pulley in a string model.

rubric.point: A peg is a fixed small support about which the string can pass.
A pulley is a wheel that can rotate as the string moves.

items.explanation: A peg is fixed and a pulley rotates. A peg must be specified as smooth before friction can be neglected.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: Explain why a uniform rigid rod can have a non-zero weight even if its shape does not change.

rubric.point: Rigid describes lack of deformation, not lack of mass.
Uniform describes even mass distribution, with weight acting through the midpoint in a uniform gravitational field.

items.explanation: Rigid and uniform describe different properties. A uniform rod may be heavy; its centre of mass is at the midpoint.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: Explain the modelling assumptions needed to use equal tension on both sides of a pulley in a connected-particle problem.

rubric.point: The string is light, so its mass is negligible.
The pulley is smooth, so friction at contact is neglected.

items.explanation: For a light string passing over a smooth pulley, tension is equal on the two sides. Light alone does not remove pulley friction.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

items.stem: Explain whether a rough wire guarantees friction acts on a stationary bead, and give a reason.

rubric.point: Roughness permits friction but does not guarantee a non-zero friction force.
Friction depends on the tendency for relative motion.

items.explanation: Rough means friction is available. If there is no tendency to slip along the wire, the friction force can be zero.
hints: Identify which property of the model matters.
Connect the stated assumption to a physical quantity.
Write the implication in the context of the object.

flashcards.back: A body with mass whose dimensions are negligible in the problem.
A flat sheet whose thickness is negligible compared with its other dimensions.
A body whose shape and size do not change under the forces considered.

flashcards.front: What do light, uniform and non-uniform mean for a rod?
flashcards.back: Light: negligible mass. Uniform: mass evenly distributed along its length. Non-uniform: mass not evenly distributed.

flashcards.front: What is a light inextensible string?
flashcards.back: A string with negligible mass whose length remains constant when taut.

flashcards.front: What is a smooth surface? What is a rough surface?
flashcards.back: A smooth surface exerts no friction; a rough surface may exert friction.

flashcards.front: What is a light smooth pulley?
flashcards.back: A pulley of negligible mass with no friction at the string contact; for a light string, tension is equal on both sides.

flashcards.front: What are a bead, wire and peg in mechanics?
flashcards.back: A bead is a small object constrained to move on a wire. A wire provides its path. A peg is a fixed small support around which a string may pass.

M1-1.1.motivate: A real car has size, a rope stretches a little, and a wheel has friction. A useful mechanics model keeps the properties that affect the question. Which of these details can you ignore in a particular calculation?

discover.stem: A light inextensible string passes over a smooth pulley. Which conclusion follows from the model?

options.A: The string has no tension because it is light.
options.B: The taut string keeps a constant length and can carry tension.
options.C: The string cannot move because it is inextensible.
options.D: The pulley cannot exert any contact force because it is smooth.

discover.explanation: Light means negligible string mass, while inextensible means constant length when taut. Smooth removes friction at contact, not tension or the contact force.

M1-1.1.establish: A particle has mass but negligible dimensions. A lamina is a flat sheet of negligible thickness. A rigid body does not change shape or size under the forces considered. A light rod or string has negligible mass; light does not mean unable to transmit force. A uniform rod has mass evenly distributed along its length and, in uniform gravity, its centre of mass is at the midpoint. A non-uniform rod has uneven mass distribution. An inextensible string keeps a constant length when taut, so connected particles have linked displacements. A smooth surface has no friction but can exert a normal reaction; a rough surface may exert friction. A light smooth pulley has negligible mass and no friction at the string contact; with a light string, tension is equal on both sides. A bead is a small object constrained to move along a wire. A wire defines its path; a peg is a fixed small support around which a string can pass. A peg or wire needs a stated smoothness assumption before friction is ignored.
M1-1.1.connect: In a later connected-particle problem, first use inextensibility to link motion, then use the light string and smooth pulley to link tensions. For a rod in a moments problem, uniformity determines where its weight acts; rigidity only tells you its shape stays fixed.
M1-1.1.note:
- Particle: mass retained, size negligible; lamina: negligible thickness; rigid body: no deformation.
- Light: negligible mass; uniform: evenly distributed mass; non-uniform: uneven mass distribution.
- Inextensible: constant taut length; smooth: no friction; rough: friction may act.
- Light smooth pulley with light string: equal tensions on both sides.
- Bead: small object constrained to a wire; peg: fixed support for a string.
M1-1.1.self_explain: A uniform rod rests on a smooth table. Which assumption places its weight at the midpoint, and which removes friction? Explain why the table can still exert a normal reaction.
